description:
Our team aims to develop a practical, data driven solution for sustainable agriculture using NASA Earth observation data, local soil information, and crop characteristics. With interests in AI, robotics, programming, and agriculture, we want to help farmers make informed decisions and adapt to changing farming conditions.

We welcome team members skilled in programming, data analysis, GIS, satellite data, agriculture, and UI/UX design.
summary:
Field Shifting: Restoring Soil, Securing Harvests
Continuous rice and wheat farming in Narowal is depleting the soil, driving up fertilizer costs, and leaving farmers exposed to floods, pests, and erratic rainfall. Field Shifting, built by team IBEXtronauts for NASA Space Apps, helps farmers rotate crops each season so their land recovers and their incomes stay secure.
Our solution has two parts. A NASA data platform evaluates rainfall, soil moisture, and temperature for each field and compares keeping the rotation, adding legumes, or changing the crop, with the likely income and risk of each. A low-cost soil testing device measures nutrients, pH, and moisture in real time, connects with NASA weather data, and has been verified through lab testing.
We will pilot the device in one or two villages, check its readings against NASA data and laboratory results, and have agricultural experts review every recommendation alongside farmers' experience. Our goal is to make smarter crop rotation practical for every farmer, starting in Narowal and expanding to more villages over time.
details:
Field Shifting is a NASA Space Apps solution developed by team IBEXtronauts to help farmers in Narowal rotate crops each season, restoring soil health while protecting their harvests and incomes. Continuous rice and wheat cultivation has depleted nutrients, raised fertilizer costs, and increased pest attacks, while floods and shifting rainfall have added further strain. NASA POWER data from 2021 to 2025 confirms these changes, making a data-driven response both urgent and practical.

Our solution has two parts. A NASA data based platform would compare keeping the current rotation, adding legumes, or changing the crop for each field, showing the likely income and risk of each option. A low-cost soil testing device would measure NPK nutrients, pH, moisture, and electrical conductivity in real time, connect with NASA weather data, and has been verified through lab testing.

We will pilot the device in one or two villages, validate its readings against NASA satellite data and laboratory results, and require agricultural expert review of every recommendation alongside farmers' field experience. In the short term, we will build capacity in NASA tools and launch an awareness service for farmers. Over three to five years, we will integrate the device with NASA data, complete laboratory certification, and expand to additional villages.

Changing crops each season can restore Narowal soil, and NASA data combined with an accessible, low-cost device can make those changes achievable for every farmer.
